Classic Brewed Black Tea

Served at: Nowruz · Feast of St. Muirgen (Lí Ban the Mermaid) · Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana)

Serves 1-2Prep 2 minCook 5 min

Tea, a beverage steeped in tradition, serves as a universal symbol of hospitality, comfort, and respect across many cultures. For Nowruz, it's a warm welcome for guests, often enjoyed with sweets. In Irish traditions, it offers solace and warmth, fitting for a feast day. During the Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana), a simple, pure cup of tea is a common and respectful offering to ancestors.

Ingredients

  • 1-2 teaspoons (5-10g) good quality loose leaf black tea, or 1-2 black tea bags
  • 2 cups (475ml) fresh, filtered water

Method

  1. Bring fresh, filtered water to a rolling boil in a kettle or saucepan.
  2. While the water is heating, warm your teapot or mug by rinsing it with a splash of hot water, then discard the water.
  3. Add the loose leaf tea or tea bags to the warmed teapot or mug.
  4. Once the water has reached a rolling boil, immediately pour it over the tea leaves or bags.
  5. Steep the tea for 3-5 minutes, depending on your desired strength. For a stronger brew, steep longer; for a lighter brew, steep less.
  6. If using loose leaf tea, strain the tea into serving cups to remove the leaves. If using tea bags, remove them from the cups.
  7. Serve hot, plain, or with accompaniments as desired for your occasion.

Tips

  • For Nowruz, serve with sugar cubes (ghand), rock candy (nabat), dates, or a slice of lemon. A pinch of cardamom can be added to the tea leaves for an aromatic touch.
  • For the Feast of St. Muirgen, serve with milk and sugar, in the traditional Irish style. It pairs wonderfully with scones or biscuits.
  • For Ullambana, serve the tea plain and unsweetened as a pure offering, symbolizing respect and clarity.
